name: Starter: Japanese
about: Japanese word order in real, everyday sentences: the verb last, and the particles that say what each word does.

words.くださる: to give (to me or us); ください: please
words.寝る: to sleep, to go to bed
words.あげる: to give (from me to someone else)
words.くれる: to give (to me, or my family or group)

douzo-yoroshiku.text: どうぞよろしくお願いします。
douzo-yoroshiku.about: Said when you meet someone, or start working with them: literally, please treat me well.

thank-you.text: ありがとうございます

am-not-is-not-are-not.en: am not, is not, are not

concept.line: は (said wa) after a word makes it what the sentence is about; English has no word for it.
です after a noun says what something is (学生です, I'm a student), and after an adjective makes it polite (高いです).
の joins two nouns, the owner or the kind first: 私の本, my book.

words.means: あります = have; ありません = do not have
います = exists, is there (people or animals); has (as in having siblings)

concept.line: か at the end makes a question, and the order stays the same; a question word sits where its answer would.

words.means: 分かります = understand; 分かりません = do not understand

concept.line: The verb, adjective or です comes at the end, before only a final particle like か; who, what, where and when all come before it.
Everyday polite verbs end in -ます, for what you do and what you will do: 行きます, I go, I'll go.

words.means: 働きます = work; 働か = work
行か = go; 行けません = cannot go; 行きません = do not go
